findings.evidence: `favoured_sub_unfavoured_eq` (line 334) has hypotheses `hq : Species.quark i ∈ C.valence h`, `hq' : Species.antiquark i ∉ C.valence h`; `IsValenceFlavor` (line 127) is `Xor`, and `favoured_pion_plus_down`/`unfavoured_pion_plus_down` (lines 610, 622) give `favoured = D(d̄)`, `unfavoured = D(d)` for the antiquark case.
findings.fix: Scope the sentence to the quark case, e.g. "...and, when the valence constituent is the quark, their difference is `D_{q_i} - D_{qbar_i}`" (or add "up to a sign").
findings.issue: Module docstring: "A flavour for which exactly one of the quark and the antiquark is a valence constituent is a `IsValenceFlavor`; for such a flavour ... their difference is the valence combination `D_{q_i} - D_{qbar_i}`." The theorem only covers the quark case; in the antiquark case the difference is `D_{qbar_i} - D_{q_i}`.

findings.evidence: `def map (ρ : Flavor → Flavor') : Species Flavor → Species Flavor'` (line 147) only renames the flavour index; `PionFlavor.swap` (Symmetries.lean:517) is documented as "The isospin reflection" and `FlavorRelation` (Symmetries.lean:188) as "the case where `ρ` exchanges the up and the down flavour".
findings.fix: Say "the isospin reflection exchanging the up and the down flavour" (as `PionFlavor.swap` and `FlavorRelation` already do) rather than "isospin rotation", in both places.
findings.issue: `Species.map`'s docstring says "A flavour symmetry of a hadron multiplet, such as an isospin rotation, acts on the species this way", and the module docstring (line 23) repeats "an isospin rotation acts on a hadron's distributions this way". `map ρ` is a relabelling of flavour labels; a general isospin rotation is not a permutation of the species index.

findings.evidence: The statement's last conjunct is `favoured ... ≠ unfavoured ...` at `z = 1/2`; `favoured_conj_of_chargeConjRelation` (line 397) shows charge conjugation does constrain `favoured`.
findings.fix: Write "so the two relations do not identify the favoured with the unfavoured combination".
findings.issue: `exists_chargeConjRelation_and_flavorRelation_favoured_ne_unfavoured`'s docstring concludes "so they leave both combinations free". The relations do constrain the combinations (e.g. `favoured_conj_of_chargeConjRelation`); what the witness shows is only that they do not identify the two with each other.

summary: Documentation is otherwise thorough and accurate, but the Symmetries module docstring attributes the valence-difference identity to every `IsValenceFlavor` when it is proved (and only true with that sign) in the quark case, and two Species docstrings call `Species.map` the action of an isospin rotation when it only models the discrete u↔d relabelling.
